title: Completion at a rational point of an essentially smooth local map
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m,L)$ and $(S,\mathfrak n,L)$ be nonzero Noetherian commutative local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism inducing the specified identity of residue fields $R/\mathfrak m=S/\mathfrak n=L$. Assume it is essentially smooth, that is, $S$ is a localization of a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map]. Set $s=\dim_L(\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_SL)$, with Kähler differentials as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then $s$ is finite and there is an isomorphism of complete local $\widehat R$-algebras
$$\widehat S\simeq\widehat R[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_s]],$$
where completions are at the maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], power series use [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and the maximal ideal on the right is $(\mathfrak m\widehat R,Z_1,\ldots,Z_s)$. This isomorphism induces the identity on $L$ and is compatible with the given map $\widehat R\to\widehat S$. In particular there is an isomorphism of graded $L$-algebras
$$\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}S\simeq(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R)[Z_1,\ldots,Z_s],$$
compatible with the base graded map, with the variables of degree one and $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R=\bigoplus_{q\geq0}\mathfrak m^q/\mathfrak m^{q+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring].

source.place: Tag 054L (lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space), followed by More on Algebra, Tag 0AGX (more-algebra.tex, lemma-flat-unramified). The displayed completion and graded formulas are the rational-residue-point consequence of these lemmas, not the verbatim statement of either tag.

proof.text: Choose a smooth algebra P whose localization is S. Contract the maximal ideal of S to a prime p of P and identify S as localization at p: elements outside p are units, and the original denominator submonoid is contained in that complement. Mathlib Algebra.IsSmoothAt.exists_isStandardEtale_mvPolynomial provides a polynomial chart on P[1/g] with g∉p. The localization map P[1/g]→S is formally etale, so composition gives an R-algebra map f:R[X_1,…,X_d]→S which is formally etale. This is the ring-level version of the normal-form step, with no scheme conversion needed.

For each chart coordinate choose a lift in R of its residue in L, using surjectivity R→R/m and the specified residue-field comparison. Precompose f with the polynomial translation X_i↦X_i−a_i, an explicitly invertible R-algebra map. The translated chart is still formally etale and sends every variable into n. Polynomial homomorphism extensionality and hres give rS(residue(f(p)))=rR(residue(constantCoeff(p))). Using the polynomial coefficient criterion at exponent one, its contracted ideal is Q=(m,X). The same residue surjectivity shows R[X]→S/n is onto.

Base-change the polynomial differential basis to S and transport it through the formally-etale differential equivalence. Base-change once more to the residue field of S. This supplies a basis indexed by Fin d, proving Module.Finite and finrank=d.

Apply the formally-etale infinitesimal-neighbourhood theorem to f and J=n. Its source ideal is Q by construction; its surjectivity hypothesis is the residue surjectivity just proved. It gives bijectivity of every positive power quotient map and the canonical associated-graded ring equivalence gS:gr_Q(R[X])→gr_n S. At exponent zero both quotients are the zero ring, hence their map is also bijective. Take inverse limits of these actual quotient maps and their inverses using AdicCompletion.liftRingHom. Compatibility with reductions is verified on polynomial representatives; coordinatewise extensionality proves that the two inverse-limit maps are inverse. This constructs eS:completion_Q(R[X])≃completion_n(S), with its evaluation formula at every n. Reuse AdicCompletion.equiv_of_powerQuotient_bijective from the shared completion-comparison module; no separate inverse-limit helper is declared here.

Apply the polynomial-model completion theorem to obtain eP:completion_Q(R[X])≃completion_m(R)[[X]]. Set e=eS⁻¹ followed by eP. The evaluation formula for eS and the constants formula for eP prove the full base-completion compatibility. At level one choose a polynomial representative for eS⁻¹(x); the residue formula for eP and the centered-chart residue equality prove that e induces the specified identity on L.

Mathlib AdicCompletion.LocalRing gives localness and maximal-ideal completeness of both maximal-ideal completions. The unit-constant-coefficient criterion for formal series gives localness of the power-series ring. Apply the combined series coefficient criterion at exponent one to identify its maximal ideal as (m completion_m(R),X); use AdicCompletion.maximalIdeal_eq_map. Every ring equivalence of local rings maps maximal ideal to maximal ideal, giving the required ideal equality for e. Transfer maximal-ideal completeness through e with IsAdicComplete.congr_ringEquiv. This also proves maximality of the displayed ideal.

Apply the polynomial-model associated-graded equivalence gP:(gr_m R)[X]≃gr_Q(R[X]) and compose with gS. The gP formula on homogeneous constant representatives and the specified equality of gS with the canonical direct-sum map prove the exact base compatibility. The gP variable formula followed by the degree-one piece map of gS gives the required degree-one classes.
